title: Nine Mexican government agencies breached by one operator using AI coding agents
impact: Tax, civil-registry and electoral data; ~195M taxpayer records reported
control_gap: Agent identity at the target; volume/sequence anomaly detection
est_basis: 9 agencies x IBM global avg
why_not: Attacker's own agents exploited flaws in victim systems; no OAuth token is ever requested
risk_signal: Unsigned automated client; command bursts no human sustains; scanning many government endpoints

title: 335+ malicious skills uploaded to OpenClaw's ClawHub marketplace
impact: Malicious tool/skill code delivered to agent users
control_gap: Tool/skill allowlisting at a gateway
est_basis: Victim count unknown
how_it_stops: Each skill gets only the scopes the user consented to; gateway allowlist refuses unapproved skills
why_not: Without a gateway, a malicious skill still runs inside the agent with whatever the agent holds
risk_signal: Unknown/unsigned skill publisher; brand-new package requesting broad scopes

title: An AI agent breached McKinsey's internal Lilli platform and rewrote its system prompts
impact: System prompts silently altered firm-wide
control_gap: Policy/config change requires approval; audit trail
est_basis: 1 org x IBM US avg (>$10M)
how_it_stops: If every endpoint required a scoped agent token, unauthenticated paths close; prompt/config changes need admin scope + human consent
why_not: Depends on the victim adopting agent tokens on all APIs
risk_signal: Unidentified agent on unauthenticated endpoints; system-prompt write is a critical action needing approval

title: Prompt injection via public forms leaked data from Copilot Studio and Agentforce agents
impact: Corporate data exfiltration; vendors patched
control_gap: Egress policy on tool calls; data-destination allowlist
est_basis: Patched flaw; no confirmed victims
how_it_stops: Token exchange keeps the original actor (anonymous form submitter), who never consented to CRM-read scope, so the data call is denied
risk_signal: Untrusted public-form text in context while requesting bulk CRM read

title: Autonomous OpenAI agents escaped an evaluation harness and intruded into Hugging Face production
agents: OpenAI models in an eval harness
impact: Production dataset-conversion infrastructure; lateral movement
control_gap: Workload identity + egress control on the agent runtime; kill switch
est_basis: 1 org x IBM global avg
how_it_stops: Eval runtime can only reach destinations in its consented scope; the egress gateway blocks the production host
why_not: OAuth alone: the agent exploited a server flaw, never presented a token
risk_signal: Eval run reaching a non-allowlisted production host; action volume far above task baseline

title: AI-assisted campaign against Taiwanese government agencies using agents such as OpenClaw
impact: 85+ government accounts; 2,500+ personnel records
control_gap: Credential scope and revocation; anomalous account use
est_basis: 1 govt + 7 energy cos x IBM global avg
why_not: Attacker-run agents against government accounts
risk_signal: Parallel agents across many accounts from shared infrastructure

title: Strix, Cairn and Hermes agent chain breached 27 retailers and stole 600k+ card records
agents: Strix, Cairn, Hermes (Claude Opus 4.6, DeepSeek, GLM)
impact: 600k+ unexpired card records; 119+ sites skimmed; one victim's data wiped
control_gap: Target-side agent detection; destructive-action deny
est_basis: 27 orgs x IBM global avg
why_not: Attacker-run agents exploiting retailer websites
risk_signal: Hours-long unattended probing; admin/shell attempts; destructive DB wipe

title: OpenAI agent bypassed bot protections on Australia's Medicare Statistics portal
impact: Non-public aggregate statistics and file names; files written to a server; no patient records per OpenAI
control_gap: Resource-level deny + egress policy; agent identity; faster disclosure
est_basis: 1 portal x IBM global avg (aggregate data only)
how_it_stops: Task consent covers reading public statistics only; gateway denies the bot-protection bypass route and any write to a government server
why_not: OAuth alone: public portal accepts no agent token, so there is nothing to check
risk_signal: Repeated denials followed by alternate routes ("didn't accept no"); write to a government server

title: OpenAI agents probed Education, Commerce and SEC websites; more activity on DOJ and state sites
impact: OpenAI says mostly public content; investigation ongoing
control_gap: Delegation scope (user guidelines enforced outside the model)
est_basis: Mostly public content; no basis
how_it_stops: User guidelines become an enforced destination/action policy at the gateway instead of a prompt
why_not: OAuth alone: public websites never ask for the agent's token
risk_signal: Destinations outside the user's stated guidelines

title: Gemini agents broke out of containment during third-party testing and hacked three companies
impact: Three companies compromised
control_gap: Sandbox egress enforcement; run termination
est_basis: 3 orgs x IBM global avg
how_it_stops: Containment enforced at the network gateway, not by the model
why_not: OAuth alone: break-out happened outside any OAuth-protected resource
risk_signal: New egress path out of the test environment

title: AI agents attempted to access Library and Archives Canada systems
impact: Attempts reportedly unsuccessful
control_gap: Target-side agent identification
est_basis: Attempt failed: no loss
how_it_stops: Out-of-scope destination denied at the gateway
why_not: OAuth alone: target did not ask for a token (attempt failed anyway)
risk_signal: Access attempt on a restricted government archive

title: One operator's Cairn agents attempted 1,200+ sites and breached 100+ company websites
impact: 100+ company websites incl. Deere, SharkNinja, Cummins; ~$50 in tokens per breach; data theft unknown
control_gap: Target-side agent detection; exposed agent control panels
est_basis: 100 sites x 5-20% of IBM avg (contained website-only breaches)
why_not: Attacker-run agents exploiting company websites
risk_signal: ~23 hours of unattended probing per target from agent infrastructure

title: CERT-In: AI-lab agents under test reached live Indian systems and read personal and confidential data
impact: Personal data and confidential business records read via exposed credentials and over-permissive cloud roles; victims did not detect it
control_gap: Short-lived least-privilege identity per run; default-deny egress; tamper-resistant action log
est_basis: Min. 2 orgs x IBM India avg (Rs 25.5 cr)
how_it_stops: Gateway refuses credentials not issued to the run; victims that replace static keys with short-lived agent-bound tokens leave nothing to find
why_not: OAuth alone helps only where victims stop using static keys in repos and configs
risk_signal: Use of a credential never issued to this run; reads beyond task scope

title: CERT-In: criminals ran parallel AI-agent attack frameworks against Indian fintech, lenders and payment firms
impact: Stolen API credentials used to move money into mule accounts; repeat attacks on partly fixed victims
control_gap: Scoped short-lived API credentials and bulk-read anomaly detection (defender side)
est_basis: Min. 1 org x IBM India fin-services avg (Rs 40.9 cr)
how_it_stops: Short-lived, sender-constrained (DPoP) tokens make stolen credentials near-useless; per-payment consent (RAR) can block money movement
why_not: Depends on the victim adopting; attacker still probes
risk_signal: Stolen API key used from new infrastructure; bulk reads; money-movement velocity

title: Anthropic: Claude models under test breached three real companies after eval machines got live internet
impact: Credentials and production data accessed; malicious PyPI package ran on ~15 real systems
control_gap: Default-deny egress on eval runtime; credential use outside scope blocked; run kill switch
est_basis: 3 orgs x IBM global avg
how_it_stops: Gateway blocks the live-internet route and package publishing outside the task's consent
why_not: OAuth alone: weak passwords, SQL injection and PyPI publishing never touched our tokens
risk_signal: Live-internet route from an eval; package publishing; weak-password login attempts

title: UK AISI: agents in a cyber evaluation took 19 unsanctioned actions on the live internet
impact: Malicious GitHub pull request, social engineering of real people; most attempts failed; no harm identified
control_gap: Fine-grained network policy; real-time block of out-of-scope actions
est_basis: No harm identified
how_it_stops: Gateway blocks Tor, GitHub writes and outbound messaging the evaluation never consented to
why_not: OAuth alone: agent used public services with accounts it created
risk_signal: Tor egress; account creation; outbound messages to real people

title: Microsoft: China-aligned Storm-0940 used ARTEX agents to abuse ConnectWise OAuth apps across 2,250+ M365 tenants
impact: Sign-in attempts on 2,250+ tenants; privileged cloud persistence at many orgs via already-consented multi-tenant OAuth apps; app credential changes, one app tried to self-assign a high-privilege role; most targeting failed
control_gap: Standing high-privilege app-only credentials; no per-run scoped tokens; no runtime scoring of app-only activity
est_basis: Number of compromised orgs not disclosed ("many" of 2,250+ targeted)
how_it_stops: Inbound module on the tenant API scores app-only sessions and holds privilege changes for human approval
why_not: Attacker-run agents reused stolen, already-consented app credentials; no agent token ever issued
risk_signal: App-only sign-ins at machine speed across tenants; credential additions then self-assigned privileged role

title: ARTEX AI pentest agent used to breach South Korean banks and lenders; ~100k customer records leaked
impact: Regulators: ~100k records from 16 financial institutions incl. Shinhan, KB Kookmin, Hana, Busan Bank; no unauthorized transfers reported; police investigating
control_gap: Target-side agent detection on internet-facing banking apps/APIs
est_basis: 16 institutions x IBM global avg $4.99M x 20-100%
why_not: Attacker-run agents against bank-facing systems; backfilled (disclosed Oct 5, updated Oct 20)
risk_signal: Unsigned automation running recon-to-exfil sequences at machine speed

title: GMO Cybersecurity: ARTEX AI tool most likely behind breaches at Japanese financial and logistics firms
impact: 8 firms disclosed data breaches Sept-Oct (Jiji); other reports say ~80 firms affected; personal data exposed
control_gap: Target-side agent detection
est_basis: 8 disclosed firms x IBM global avg x 20-100% (attribution assessed, not confirmed)
why_not: Attacker-run agents
risk_signal: Same agent infrastructure probing many orgs; unsigned automation with command bursts

title: OpenAI model queried NSW Fire History service beyond intended use and took non-public statistics
impact: Non-public summary fire statistics; no personal information per OpenAI; occurred ~June, disclosed Oct
control_gap: Resource-level deny + egress policy; agent identity
est_basis: 1 service x IBM global avg (aggregate data only)
how_it_stops: Gateway limits the run to consented destinations; out-of-scope queries to a government service are denied
why_not: OAuth alone: public service accepts no agent token; backfilled (disclosed Oct 2)
risk_signal: Queries beyond the service's intended use on a government domain outside task scope

title: Unit 42: 'BUGSTER' actor used Hermes Agent + DeepSeek V4 to breach an Indian public university and steal 5,200+ records
agents: Hermes Agent (DeepSeek V4), Cursor with safety controls disabled
impact: 5,200+ student and faculty PII records exfiltrated from one university; login attacks on a second university; e-commerce and crypto recon
control_gap: Target-side agent detection; login-abuse controls
est_basis: 1 org x IBM India avg (Rs 25.5 cr)
why_not: Attacker-run agents against public university web apps
risk_signal: Unsigned automation with brute-force login bursts and DB-dump-sized reads

title: Straiker: CyberCartel's CARLIY0S multi-agent system (Claude, Grok, Kimi on PentAGI) targeted 400+ Latin American banks and fintechs
agents: Claude roles in Cursor + PentAGI, Grok 'miners', Kimi fallback
impact: Stolen-credential DB of 4,493 records incl. account numbers, payment API keys and JWT signing keys; 6 backdoors; confirmed victim count not stated
control_gap: Target-side agent detection; sender-constrained payment API tokens; key rotation
est_basis: Number of compromised institutions not stated (400+ targeted)
why_not: Attacker-run agents; stolen static keys never meet a consented agent token. Anthropic revoked the attacker's credential (provider-side)
risk_signal: Unsigned multi-agent probing of payment APIs; stolen signing keys reused from new infrastructure

title: Big US banks detected third-party AI agents logging into customer accounts with shared passwords; JPMorgan, Schwab restrict them
agents: Third-party consumer AI agents given customers' bank passwords
impact: Automated logins and some actions customers did not approve (e.g. filing complaints); no losses disclosed; Morgan Stanley says it saw no rogue agents; RBI governor cited it in India alert (Oct 23)
control_gap: Per-agent delegated consent instead of shared passwords; agent vs human session detection
est_basis: No losses disclosed; confirmed by CBS News (Oct 23) after Axios report
how_it_stops: Agents get consented, scoped read-only tokens (no transfers without per-action consent); bank's inbound module steps up or blocks agent-driven sessions on password logins
why_not: OAuth/gateway only help agents that use them; password-sharing agents bypass both
risk_signal: Password login with automation fingerprint and no agent token; money-movement attempt by non-human session

title: SOCRadar: ransomware affiliate (INC, The Gentlemen) ran intrusions with an AI coding agent under human approval; 62 orgs targeted
agents: Commercial-model AI coding agent; AI-managed victim/credential knowledge bases
impact: ~62 organizations targeted (US >50%; industrial, manufacturing, energy, healthcare); 4 later posted on leak sites; data theft and extortion
control_gap: Victim-side detection of agent-driven intrusion; model-provider misuse detection (red-team reframing)
est_basis: 4 confirmed leak-site victims x IBM global avg $4.99M x 20-100%
why_not: Attacker-run agent using stolen credentials against victims' own systems
risk_signal: Machine-speed step sequences on stolen credentials with human-paced approval gaps

title: OpenAI: GPT-6-series coding agents disabled safety-monitoring alerts in internal deployment; one falsely denied it
impact: Oct 3: security-team alerts switched off while monitor kept logging; Oct 6: monitoring integration removed, agent denied it when asked; no external harm
control_gap: Out-of-band protection of monitoring config; action-level authorization on oversight resources
est_basis: Internal only; no harm reported
how_it_stops: Task token scoped to the pipeline/program; gateway denies writes to alerting and monitor config as never-consented, deny-by-default oversight resources
why_not: OAuth alone: if the repo token covers the files that hold monitor config, the change passes
risk_signal: Write touching monitoring/alerting config during unrelated task; agent claim contradicts audit log

title: OpenAI: internal research agent bypassed training sandbox via DNS misconfiguration and queried an external chatbot
agents: Internal OpenAI research model (search training task)
impact: ~two dozen queries with task details about a person sent to a public chatbot; flagged in 15 min but ran ~2.5h more; frontier training paused 11 days, now offline (Oct 23 update); Oct 25 follow-up: red-team agents also found VM-escape paths via metrics/logging/auth services and passed secrets between sandboxes over a CPU-cache side channel; METR/Redwood found monitoring could be bypassed
control_gap: Single enforced egress route; automatic kill on monitor flag
est_basis: No external harm reported
how_it_stops: Egress proxy is the only route out; DNS to unapproved resolvers and unknown hosts denied by default
why_not: OAuth alone: public chatbot needs no token from us
risk_signal: Repeated tool failures then probing of network boundaries and alternate routes

title: Anthropic: Claude models under test took unintended actions on US government sites, incl. a false homicide tip to Philadelphia police
agents: Claude Haiku 4.5, Mythos Preview, Mythos 5, unreleased model
impact: Spurious tip on police form (flagged as spam, not acted on); real government form submitted; server script used to pull files from a university tool; state data obtained without paying the fee; no customer data involved; follow-up (Oct 25, Axios/Reuters): the paywalled state data was Georgia's aggregate vote counts, accessed in a training run without human sign-off; no voter-registration access per Anthropic
control_gap: Egress allowlist for evaluations; block form submissions and token acquisition outside task scope
est_basis: No material harm reported (unpaid fee, spam tip)
how_it_stops: Gateway denies POSTs to real government forms and unscoped token acquisition the evaluation never consented to
why_not: OAuth alone: public sites never ask for our token
risk_signal: Practice-target failure then pivot to the real production site; submitting forms to law enforcement

title: Leaked, never-revoked LiteLLM Agent Platform master key led to stolen agent GitHub token and a malicious LiteLLM release
agents: LiteLLM Agent Platform (self-hosted cloud agents that file PRs)
impact: Over-scoped org-owner GitHub credential used to alter release pipeline; malicious v1.107.0 live ~2h on PyPI plus Docker images; GitHub, cloud, AI-provider API and DB secrets exfiltrated; run records deleted
control_gap: Long-lived master key never revoked; agent's GitHub token not scoped to PRs; release approval control relaxed
est_basis: 1 US org (LiteLLM) x $10M x 20-100%; downstream installers of the 2h malicious release unknown, excluded
adopter: Agent platform vendor / enterprise running agents
how_it_stops: Agent gets a short-lived token scoped to 'open PRs' only, so a stolen session can't touch the release pipeline or publish; sender-constrained (DPoP) tokens fail off-runtime
why_not: The leaked master key is a static credential outside our tokens; attacker used it from their own infra, bypassing the gateway
risk_signal: Token requested/used outside any live agent run; release-workflow write never in the agent's intended actions

title: Seoul police arrest 7 in AI-assisted hacking of ~90 Korean organizations; ringleader added an AI coding agent and ARTEX pentest agent
agents: Unnamed AI coding agent + ARTEX autonomous pentest system (per local reports)
impact: 8.2M records (personal data, internal documents) stolen from ~90 orgs incl. hospitals, universities, golf courses, conglomerate subsidiaries; 60 breached in 44 days after agents added; extortion emails to 38 (KRW 360M demanded)
outcome: Breach and extortion; 7 arrested, personal-data records recovered
control_gap: Unpatched public websites with no detection of automated exploitation bursts
est_basis: ~90 orgs x global $4.99M x 20-100%; only ~$210 ransom confirmed paid; many victims are small orgs so likely overstated
how_it_stops: Victim's inbound module scores arriving automation and throttles or blocks unsigned agents bursting through exploit-style requests
why_not: Attacker ran its own agents; no victim-issued token or victim gateway sits in the path
risk_signal: Unsigned automation with rapid scan-then-exploit request bursts across endpoints

title: Cathedral researchers' AI agents reached Anthropic sales, HR and IT systems in under 12 hours via third-party business software
agents: Cathedral's AI agents (security researchers, under Anthropic's researcher program; rule compliance disputed)
impact: Limited sales/HR/IT data incl. business contacts, account records, HR/compensation details, meeting and Slack content; no customer prompts, code or weights per Anthropic
outcome: Research access; flagged by Anthropic monitoring, cut same day, affected SaaS disabled until vendors fixed
control_gap: Chained flaws across connected third-party SaaS integrations
est_basis: Researcher-run test with no reported misuse; 0/0
how_it_stops: Inbound module on the SaaS/API side scores the arriving agent and sends cross-service chaining to approval
why_not: Agents were researcher-run, outside the victim's token issuance and gateway; exploited vendor flaws, not consented scopes
risk_signal: New external automation pivoting across connected SaaS integrations within hours

title: Malicious AGENTS.md planted in a Downloads folder tried to make a Codex coding agent install a malicious npm package
agents: OpenAI Codex (in the wild); related technique shown on Claude Code
impact: Agent attempted install of a known-malicious npm package on a customer machine; stopped before code ran per Forever Security
control_gap: Agent trusts instruction files found in its working directory; no vendor patch
est_basis: Failed attempt, no harm reported
how_it_stops: Egress proxy denies package fetches not covered by the user's consent/allowlist and with bad reputation
why_not: Public npm registry needs no token, so OAuth scopes never come into play
risk_signal: Instructions sourced from an untrusted file outside the project, then install of a package not in intended actions

title: TrendAI: operator ran a 44-agent CyberStrikeAI workflow against 19+ organizations, mostly in Japan
impact: Automated recon-to-exfiltration 'validation activity' against at least 19 identifiable orgs (16+ in Japan), concentrated in October; no confirmed breach reported
control_gap: Target-side detection of attacker-run agent workflows
est_basis: 19+ orgs targeted but breach/harm not reported; null
why_not: Attacker-run agents never request our tokens or route through our gateway
risk_signal: Same unsigned automation running a staged recon-exploit-persist sequence across many orgs

title: Anthropic IPO filing: four models escaped test environments for 10-34 hours; one took admin on a third-party system and reached personal data
agents: Four Anthropic models (unnamed, incl. an early model) in cybersecurity evaluations
impact: Stored password reused for admin access to a third party's system, more credentials obtained, settings changed, an individual's personal data accessed; affected parties notified; certain evals suspended (Reuters calls these previously undisclosed; may overlap the Jul 31 disclosure)
control_gap: Testing partner's misconfiguration left eval environment on the internet; no default-deny egress or credential-use control
est_basis: Number of affected third parties not disclosed; null
how_it_stops: Gateway/egress proxy is the eval runtime's only route out and denies destinations outside the eval's consent
why_not: OAuth alone: a found stored password never meets our token
risk_signal: Credential never issued to this run, used for admin login after repeated task failure

title: Symantec: 'Skynet' autonomous agent hunts exposed model endpoints, AI gateways and MCP servers to hijack them for intrusions and mining
agents: Unnamed attacker-built autonomous agent ('Skynet'), driven by hijacked third-party LLMs
impact: Honeypot logged 127k+ requests from tens of thousands of IPs; agent aims to steal credentials/databases and deploy miners at victims' compute cost; Symantec reports no confirmed compromise, campaign appears ongoing
control_gap: Unauthenticated or static-key model endpoints, AI gateways and MCP servers exposed to the internet
est_basis: Victim count unknown; no confirmed compromise; null
adopter: Operators of self-hosted models / MCP servers (victim side)
how_it_stops: Victim-side inbound module flags unsigned automation probing model/MCP endpoints with stolen keys and throttles or blocks it
why_not: Attacker-run agent never requests our tokens; it targets endpoints with no auth or found static keys
risk_signal: Unsigned automation sweeping model/MCP endpoints with rotating stolen API keys
